title: UiPath Pricing 2026: License Cost, Robots From $1,450 a Year
summary: UiPath pricing structures are broken down here to help you evaluate total ownership costs and identify suitable alternatives for your automation needs.
body_markdown:
## UiPath alternatives for enterprise automation compared


### Microsoft Power Automate: The bundled alternative


If you're already operating within the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, Microsoft Power Automate has a lower barrier to entry because it uses existing identity management and data connectors.


This integration means you can grant automation permissions through the Microsoft Entra ID portal. This is the same interface used for standard email and file access.


Power Automate allows you to create flows directly in a web browser, reducing the local hardware requirements for your departmental developers.


While UiPath requires specialized Studio software for complex builds, the Microsoft platform relies heavily on the Power Platform environment. If you're automating legacy desktop applications, you must still license per-user or per-flow credits to access the necessary "premium" connectors.


### Activepieces: The open-source and developer-friendly choice


Activepieces provides granular usage visibility across 739+ integrations, allowing teams to set hard cost caps per project or person to prevent the unpredictable credit depletion common in consumption models.


The following table outlines how the UiPath 2024 tiers distribute resources, highlighting the jump from individual learning to governed enterprise scale:


Feature Free Tier Pro ($420/mo Developer) Enterprise (Custom)


Orchestrator Access Shared Community Cloud Dedicated Tenant Multiple Production Tenants


Support Level Community Forum Standard (Email) 24/7 Premium / Mission Critical


Robot Types 2 Attended / 1 Unattended 1 Attended / 1 Unattended Unlimited Scalability


As soon as you require a dedicated production environment, this tiered structure demonstrates that the cost shifts from a flat software fee to a managed platform commitment.


### Transparent pricing for scalable workflows


At the million-page mark, the $150,000 price tag costs several multiples more than calling Mistral OCR 4.1 or Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite directly, suggesting that direct API integration offers a far more efficient path for budget-conscious organizations.


Unlike UiPath’s thousands-of-dollars entry point, the platform uses a task-based credit system where you only pay for what you execute.


For larger organizations, the Enterprise self-hosted version moves away from per-task billing to a flat annual fee based on the number of users or instances.


This allows you to run millions of automations on your own hardware without the per-execution tax that makes UiPath cost-prohibitive at scale.


By allowing you to self-host the entire stack on your own infrastructure, Activepieces avoids this specific escalation.


The enterprise feature list (including SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, and audit logs) is identical in the self-hosted air-gapped documentation and the managed cloud, ensuring that regulated organizations do not lose control for the sake of functionality.


This setup ensures that data never leaves your corporate firewall. Because it uses a TypeScript-based framework, your software engineer can write custom logic using Gemini 3.8 Flash to generate specific automation scripts. They aren't restricted to the pre-built activities found in a proprietary library.


MoneyGram and Moneypenny run Activepieces in production to maintain this level of architectural flexibility while scaling their automation efforts.


### Automation Anywhere: The direct legacy competitor


Automation Anywhere is the primary alternative for you if you require a web-based, cloud-native architecture for large-scale Robotic Process Automation. Unlike the thick-client installation required for UiPath Studio, the Automation 360 platform runs entirely in a browser.


At the million-page mark, the $150,000 price tag costs several multiples more than calling Mistral OCR 4.1 or Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite directly, rendering the choice of vendor a critical factor in project profitability.


It maintains a similar focus on "Digital Workers," which are licensed as discrete units of labor to perform repetitive back-office tasks.


While the interface is designed to be accessible to business analysts, the underlying complexity of its Control Room demands a dedicated infrastructure team to oversee security and bot scheduling.
